solved.topic: First law of thermodynamics - work done
solved.q: A system absorbs 2000 J of heat and its internal energy increases by 1500 J. Find the work done by the system.
steps: Answer: work done by the system = 500 J (positive, so work is done by the gas on surroundings).

solved.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally at 300 K from a volume of 1 L to 10 L. Calculate the work done by the gas. (R = 8.314 J/mol K)
steps: Given: n = 2 mol, T = 300 K, V1 = 1 L, V2 = 10 L.
Formula: W = nRT ln(V2/V1) = 2.303 nRT log10(V2/V1).

solved.topic: Adiabatic process - change in internal energy
solved.q: A gas undergoes an adiabatic process and does 150 J of work on its surroundings. Find the change in its internal energy.
steps: Given: dQ = 0 (adiabatic), dW = 150 J (work done by gas).
Formula: dQ = dU + dW, so dU = dQ - dW = -dW (since dQ = 0).
Answer: internal energy decreases by 150 J (gas cools, since it used its own internal energy to do work).

solved.topic: Work done at constant pressure (area under P-V curve)
solved.q: A gas at constant pressure 2 x 10^5 Pa expands from a volume of 2 L to 5 L. Calculate the work done by the gas.
steps: Formula: W = P(V2 - V1), since P is constant, this equals the area under the P-V curve.

solved.topic: Carnot engine efficiency and work done
solved.q: A Carnot engine operates between a source at 600 K and a sink at 300 K. If it absorbs 840 J of heat from the source, find its efficiency and the work done per cycle.
steps: Formula: eta = 1 - T2/T1 and W = eta x Q1.
Answer: efficiency = 50%, work done per cycle = 420 J.

solved.q: A Carnot refrigerator maintains a cold chamber at 250 K while rejecting heat to surroundings at 300 K. Calculate its coefficient of performance.
steps: Answer: COP = 5 (no unit, it is a ratio).

solved.topic: Heat engine - efficiency from Q1 and Q2
solved.q: A heat engine absorbs 1500 J of heat from a hot reservoir and its efficiency is 30%. Find the work done and the heat rejected to the cold reservoir.
steps: Formula: eta = W/Q1, so W = eta x Q1; also Q1 = W + Q2, so Q2 = Q1 - W.
Answer: work done = 450 J, heat rejected = 1050 J.

solved.q: A monatomic gas (gamma = 5/3) at an initial pressure of 3.2 x 10^5 Pa and volume 1 L expands adiabatically to a volume of 8 L. Find the final pressure.
steps: Given: P1 = 3.2 x 10^5 Pa, V1 = 1 L, V2 = 8 L, gamma = 5/3.
Formula: P1 V1^gamma = P2 V2^gamma, so P2 = P1 (V1/V2)^gamma.

practice.q: A gas absorbs 1200 J of heat and its internal energy increases by 900 J. Find the work done by the gas.
practice.hint: dQ = dU + dW, so dW = dQ - dU.

practice.q: 1 mole of an ideal gas at 400 K expands isothermally from 2 L to 20 L. Find the work done (R = 8.314 J/mol K, log10(10) = 1).
In an adiabatic compression, 200 J of work is done on a gas. Find the change in internal energy.
practice.hint: dQ = 0, so dU = -dW; work done ON the gas means dW (by gas) = -200 J.

practice.q: A gas at constant pressure 1 x 10^5 Pa is compressed from 6 L to 4 L. Find the work done by the gas.
practice.hint: W = P(V2 - V1); compression gives negative work done by gas.

practice.q: A Carnot engine works between 500 K and 400 K. If it absorbs 1000 J of heat, find its efficiency and heat rejected.
practice.hint: eta = 1 - T2/T1; Q2 = Q1(1 - eta) = Q1 x T2/T1.

practice.q: A Carnot refrigerator operates between 263 K and 303 K. Find its coefficient of performance.
practice.hint: COP = T2/(T1 - T2) with T2 the cold reservoir.
